subject: Response-time guarantee carveout for Greenfield onboarding
messages:
From: Elena Campos <elena@greenfield.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+contracts@greenfield.ai
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: response-time guarantees and temporary carveout request

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. We're excited to move forward with Redwood for our hosted inference needs. A couple of items came up from our security/procurement team that I'd like to get aligned on before we sign:

- Greenfield will ramp traffic quickly during our pilot (expected 3x baseline in first 30 days). Our legal team asked whether we can get a short-term exception for the p95 response-time guarantee while we allow for the onboarding burst.
- Specifically: request a 30-day carveout where p95 is measured on a relaxed threshold (we'd accept a 10% grace over the contracted p95) while we finalize traffic shaping and KV-cache warmups.
- We also need clarity on the measurement window for p50/p95 (rolling 30m vs fixed 1h) and whether transient retry/backoff behavior is excluded from the measurement.

Can you confirm the process to request a temporary carveout and what evidence Redwood needs? I'll loop in procurement if you want.

Best,
Elena
Elena Campos
Head of Platform — Greenfield.ai

Attachment: Greenfield_onboarding_summary.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Campos <elena@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: response-time guarantees and temporary carveout request

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the context. We can support a short-term carveout during pilot but we need a mutually-agreed scope and measurable controls. Proposed approach: 

1) Carveout window: 30 calendar days starting on go-live (we can agree on the start timestamp in the mutual action plan).
2) Relaxation: p95 threshold offset capped at +10% in the carveout window; p50 remains contractual.
3) Measurement: rolling 30-minute quantile window for p50/p95, sampled at 1s resolution across all ingress points. Transient retries from client-side exponential backoff will be excluded if they carry a 429/503 retry header — we will ingest the x-redwood-retry header to filter out retry-triggered requests from the measurement sample.
4) Evidence: for audit we will produce a carveout report daily (CSV) showing sampled latencies, request distributions, and cache hit rates. We'll need Greenfield to share expected ramp schedule and the initial traffic shape (sample traces or histograms).

I've looped Priyom (serving runtime) and Lauren (contracts) to confirm technical feasibility and to draft the carveout addendum. If that all sounds reasonable, I can circulate a short addendum and a checklist for the operational handoff.

On the measurement window question: our standard is rolling 30min for hosted customers on this tier. If Greenfield needs a different aggregation (e.g., 1h fixed epoch) we can discuss the implications — rolling windows are better for mitigating burst volatility.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_slo-matrix.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Elena Campos <elena@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: response-time guarantees and temporary carveout request

Marissa / Elena —

Quick technical notes from the serving team: 

- We can implement the x-redwood-retry header parsing to exclude client-initiated retry loops from p95 sampling. Please have Greenfield include that header on retried attempts; we will default to counting only first-attempts otherwise.
- For the 30-day carveout, we propose the following operational controls to keep the service stable and minimize customer impact:
  * Auto-throttle rule: if p95 exceeds contracted + 25% for more than 15m we will engage burst-mitigation (rate-limiter adjustments and temporary GC-friendly quant path).
  * Traffic shaping assistance: our SREs can provision a short-lived dedicated pool (best-effort) to absorb the pilot burst; this is not billed as Dedicated but will incur an overage estimate we can pre-approve.
  * KV-cache warmup: we'll run a warmup job for the first 48h to prefill common prefixes if Greenfield provides a seed corpus (preferred).
- Measurement nuance: rolling 30m with sample rate 100% on p50, p95 computed with weighted sliding-window to avoid staircase artifacts during rapid ramp. We will include both raw samples and downsampled histograms in the daily carveout reports.

If Greenfield agrees to the headers and seed corpus, the carveout is operationally straightforward. Happy to set a quick call to walk through the warmup instrumentation.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Campos <elena@greenfield.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+contracts@greenfield.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2025 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding: response-time guarantees and temporary carveout request

Marissa / Priyom —

Appreciate the thorough writeup. Greenfield accepts the 30-day carveout with the +10% p95 relaxation, rolling 30-minute measurement, and the retry-header exclusion approach. We'll supply:

- Seed corpus (S3 link) for KV warmup by Thursday.
- Ramp schedule CSV with expected qps per hour for the first 30 days.
- Agreement to add the x-redwood-retry header on retried attempts.

Next steps from Redwood: please circulate the one-page carveout addendum (including daily report format) and the estimated overage cost for the temporary dedicated pool so procurement can approve. Once we have the addendum and the DocuSign link, procurement will sign within 48 business hours.

Thanks — looking forward to go-live next week.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform, Greenfield.ai
